answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil farms by making reputation a delayed, capital-backed lattice. Every newcomer locks a copper bond that cannot be withdrawn until a trellis of already-established peers has independently verified live work across several epochs. A single whisper of support from a brand-new clone does not count: only attesters who still have skin in the game can add an edge, and edges decay unless refreshed by real service. Fabricating a dense enough graph costs more than the short-term reward of stuffing the rolls.
